title: Denied? Do These 5 Things in the First 7 Days — Reel
description: Most people who get an insurance denial never appeal at all. The real appeal letter template regulators publish, plus the deadline that catches people off guard.
sourceCitation: 180-day federal appeal window: U.S. Department of Labor, 29 CFR § 2560.503-1. Florida property insurance deadlines under Fla. Stat. §§ 627.70131 and 627.70132 (2022 reform legislation). NAIC official sample appeal letter template. This video uses AI-generated narration. Educational content only, not legal or insurance advice.

scenes.narrationText: Most people who get denied never appeal at all. Insurance companies know that. Here's exactly what to do in the first seven days, before your window closes.

find.text: The reason for this determination is

scenes.narrationText: Step one: find the exact reason, not the summary. Insurers deny for one narrow line — "not medically necessary," "pre-existing condition," "missing documentation."
Step five: put it in writing, always — phone calls disappear. And here's the letter nobody shows you: this is the National Association of Insurance Commissioners' own published template.

find.text: I am writing to request a review of your denial

scenes.narrationText: Not a law firm's marketing page. The actual regulator's format.

find.text: The reason for denial was listed as

scenes.narrationText: Your deadline depends on where you live. In California, health insurers must decide your internal appeal within thirty days — five for urgent cases — and you have the right to an independent medical review if that fails.

visual.label: CALIFORNIA INTERNAL APPEAL DECISION — PLUS THE RIGHT TO INDEPENDENT MEDICAL REVIEW

scenes.narrationText: In Florida, property insurers must pay or deny your claim within sixty days, and you have one year from the date of loss to file. Both of those Florida rules date to 2022 reform legislation — still current law, still catch people off guard.

visual.label: FLORIDA PAY-OR-DENY DEADLINE — 1 YEAR TO FILE FROM DATE OF LOSS (2022 REFORM LAW)
